content.text:
Investigate how filaments and spools should be handled in JusPrin, and write a proposal: current behaviour, the problems, options, and a recommendation. Don't implement until the direction is agreed.

What prompted it (2026-09-25, live-testing the Home printer-card redesign on branch claude/printer-card-messaging-906fb4):
- Home's printer cards have a "Loaded" row (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx, filled in `OrcaHomeBackend::printers()` in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp). For a connected Bambu printer it lists the AMS trays the device reports, via `PrinterSetup::discover_printers()` spools. Otherwise it lists `Workspace::SpoolStore::spools_for(printer_name)`.
- In a fresh data dir, three printers were added and never given spools by the person. Each card still showed a "PLA" spool in teal, the project's current filament colour; the header chip read "Teal PLA". The shell records a spool automatically when a printer is selected: see the "seed" code in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp, around lines 340 and 435 (`seed.colour = colour`, `spool.colour = colour`). The card redesign's rule is that every line rests on something verified. An auto-recorded project filament shown as "Loaded" on a printer breaks that rule.

Map the whole picture:
- `Workspace::SpoolStore` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/SpoolStore.hpp): what a spool is, and who writes to the store and when. That includes StatusRow seeding, the spool chip and menu (Shell/SpoolMenu.cpp), the printer setup conversation (`OrcaPrinterBackend::change_printer` with spools), rename and remove of printers, and connected-printer trays.
- How Orca's own filament presets and per-extruder colours in the project relate to spools. Also the Bambu AMS trays (DevFilaSystem), and what the setup chat tells the model about spools (AgentUI printerInstructions.ts).
- What each surface shows: the header spool chip, the spool menu, Home cards, the printer panel, and the Agent context.

Questions to answer:
1. Should the app record spools on its own (seeding), or only when the person says so or a printer reports them? If it seeds, how is a seeded spool marked, and should Home show it?
2. One source of truth per printer: device trays versus remembered spools versus project filament. What should win when they disagree, and what shows when a Bambu printer goes offline?
3. Spools without a colour, or without a material: how are they stored and shown?
4. The relationship to future Spoolman support. The Home card handoff lists Spoolman as out of scope.

Deliver the proposal in the final message. Include the data flow as it is now, the specific code locations, options with trade-offs, a recommendation, and how you would verify it. The shell harness can build Home cards through the real backend: `home_card()` in tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp.

  'Use plain language, one to three short sentences. Ask one question at a time, and say where to find any answer you ask ' +
  'for. Avoid internal terms such as profile, preset and catalog.\n' +
  'When the person plainly states what to do or what changed ("I put a 0.6 nozzle on it", "yes, add it", "put it back ' +
  'to 0.4"), do it: call the tool without asking again. When you are guessing -- which model from a photo or a vague ' +
  'description, which printer on the network -- ask first and stop: that reply calls no ' +
  'tool, and you act on the person\'s answer. ' +
  'After a tool result, say what happened in the person\'s terms. Never say something is done before a tool says so. ' +
  'Write every fact from the tools and the facts below, never from memory. Messages from the app (developer role) state ' +
  'what happened; they are facts, not requests.\n' +
  'Answers to tap: whenever your message asks a yes-or-no question, asks the person to confirm something, or asks ' +
  'them to pick from a few options, its last line must be "Choices: first | second | third" -- two to four short ' +
  'answers, each under 30 characters, written as the person would say them. The person taps one instead of typing, ' +
  'and it reaches you as their own message. Leave the line out only when you need free text, such as an address or ' +
  'a model name, and never write anything after it. Examples:\n' +
  'From your photo, that looks like the Anycubic Kobra 3. Is that it?\nChoices: Yes, that is it | Different printer\n' +
  'Which one is yours?\nChoices: Prusa MK4 | Prusa MK4S | Prusa MK4S HF\n' +
  'Rules for finding the printer:\n' +
  '- Start with just the printer model. Do not ask for nozzle, plate or filament first; the plate and filament are ' +
  'chosen when preparing a print.\n' +
  '- The person names one model plainly: call printer_identify with it, then add it with printer_add, with the nozzle ' +
  'it ships with unless they said another. Then say which nozzle it was set up with and that you can change it if ' +
  'theirs is different. One model fits a photo or a vague description: show it with printer_identify and ask if that ' +
  'is it. ' +
  'Two or three genuinely fit: call it with all of them and ask which, one choice each. More than three fit: do not ' +
  'call it; ask one question that narrows it down, or offer to browse the full list (printer_manual_setup). Nothing ' +
  "fits, or it isn't a filament printer: say so, offer the full list, and never offer a closest substitute.\n" +

  'begins Prusa MK4, MK4S and MK4S HF, so it is three printers.\n' +
  '- A photo names a model only from a readable name or printed size; going by shape alone, ask for a photo of the ' +
  'label. Never judge size from how big it looks. A clone uses the model it copies.\n' +
  '- Pass a nozzle only when the person or a photo said its size, and never substitute a size they did not confirm. ' +
  'After unknown_nozzle, name the sizes supported for that model and ask them to check the marking on the nozzle.\n' +
  '- alreadyYours means settings for the same model were saved before, not that this machine was added.\n' +
  'Rules for changing a printer:\n' +
  '- Work out what physically changed and change only that with printer_change; afterwards say what that means ("Every ' +
  'project that uses the K1 now slices for 0.6 mm."). If what changed is unclear, ask. Putting it back is the same tool.\n' +
  "- The plate belongs to each project, not the printer. Nozzle material, such as hardened steel, isn't tracked.\n" +
  '- A nozzle mismatch reported by the printer is something to offer to fix with printer_change.\n' +
  'Rules for connecting a printer:\n' +

content.text:
I've written the proposal below and changed no code. Line numbers refer to the `claude/printer-card-messaging-906fb4` worktree, including its uncommitted card-redesign changes, because this worktree is on an older main that has no `JusPrin/Shell` or `Workspace`.

# Filaments and spools in JusPrin: proposal

## 1. Current behaviour

### What a spool is
A `Workspace::Spool` ([SpoolStore.hpp:26](../printer-card-messaging-906fb4/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/SpoolStore.hpp:26)) has these fields: `printer_preset`, `filament_preset` (an Orca preset name), `colour` (`#RRGGBB`), `name`, `brand` and `last_used`. It is saved to `<data_dir>/jusprin/spools.json`. There is no material field (material is looked up from the preset) and no record of where the spool came from. The file loader requires `colour`, but an empty string is accepted.

### Who writes to the store

| Writer | Where | When |
|---|---|---|
| **Seeding** | [StatusRow.cpp:336-347](../printer-card-messaging-906fb4/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:336) `current_spool()` | On every `refresh_chip()`, which runs on every project-state change, and on every `listed_spools()`. If the selected printer has no spools, it adds one built from the project's filament preset and `filament_colour`. The comment at :350 ("Nothing here writes") is wrong. |
| Spool menu "Use this spool" | [SpoolMenu.cpp:418-427](../printer-card-messaging-906fb4/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/SpoolMenu.cpp:418) | The person picks a compatible preset, a colour and a name. |
| Spool menu recolour, rename, remove, touch | SpoolMenu.cpp:93, 170, 186, 219 | Explicit person actions. |
| `remember_spool()` | StatusRow.cpp:429 | Only the harness calls it. |
| Setup chat `printer_change` with spools | [OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:170-182](../printer-card-messaging-906fb4/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:170) | Deletes all of the printer's spools, then adds the model's list. **It stores the model's `material` text ("PLA") in `filament_preset`.** |
| Rename a printer | [NamedPrinters.cpp:241](../printer-card-messaging-906fb4/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp:241) `move_printer` | The rename also temporarily *selects* the printer (:232), which runs seeding. |
| Remove a printer | NamedPrinters.cpp:288 `remove_printer` | Removing the selected printer selects the system preset it inherits from (:272), which seeds a spool under that system preset's name. Nothing ever cleans that spool up. I inferred this from the code and have not run it yet. |

Connected-printer trays never go into the store. [PrinterDiscovery.cpp:39-59](../printer-card-messaging-906fb4/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterDiscovery.cpp:39) reads `DevFilaSystem` AMS trays and `vt_slot` into `DiscoveredPrinter::spools`, each with a name ("Bambu PLA Matte"), a colour (empty when the printer reported none) and a material type.

### How Orca's filament relates to spools
- Orca keeps one filament preset per extruder in `preset_bundle->filament_presets` and per-extruder colours in `project_config.filament_colour`.
- The chip reads only extruder 0 (`SetupCommands::current_filament` / `current_colour`, SetupCommands.cpp:82-105). There is a TODO(slice 2) for multi-extruder printers at StatusRow.cpp:357.
- Choosing a spool writes into the project: its preset, then its colour. Nothing flows back from the project to spools, apart from seeding.
- JusPrin does not expose Orca's own AMS-to-project sync (`Sidebar::sync_ams_list`).

### What each surface shows

| Surface | Source |
|---|---|
| **Header chip** (StatusRow.cpp:352) | Printer nickname. On the right, the name of the stored spool that matches the project's preset *and* colour, otherwise the filament's alias. The dot always shows the *project* colour. "Teal PLA" was the seeded spool's name. |
| **Spool menu** | The store's spools for the current printer. A tick marks the one `current()` matches. |
| **Home card "Loaded"** ([OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:266-273, 330-336](../printer-card-messaging-906fb4/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:330)) | A connected device's trays. **Otherwise the store's spools**, shown as `filament_type(preset)` plus colour. `SpoolEntry` has no name and no record of where it came from. |
| **Printer panel / setup chat** ([OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:93-107](../printer-card-messaging-906fb4/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:93), [printerInstructions.ts:88-91](../printer-card-messaging-906fb4/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts:88)) | "Spools loaded:" comes from device trays when connected, otherwise from the store, with `material` filled from `filament_preset`. The prompt has no rules about spools. The `printer_change` schema says "the complete list of spools loaded now". |
| **Project Agent** | Sees the project's printer and filament presets (AgentHost.cpp:468) and device trays through the `printers` tool (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1500). Its mismatch check compares project filament types with device trays (ToolResults.cpp:321). **It never sees remembered spools.** |

## 2. Problems

1. **Seeding makes project state look like printer state.** Adding a printer selects it, the chip refreshes, and the printer gets "Teal PLA". This explains your three cards. The seeded spool can't be told apart from one the person named. The setup chat then tells the model "Spools loaded: Teal PLA", so the model repeats it as fact.
2. **Reading the chip writes to the store.** Transient selections during rename and remove create spools, including probable orphans under system presets.
3. **An offline Bambu printer falls back to the store**, so it shows the seed (or old chat-written spools) as "Loaded". A connected printer's trays are never kept.
4. **The chat path stores the wrong kind of value.** `filament_preset = "PLA"` has these effects:
   - Home's `filament_type("PLA")` finds no preset, so the card loses the material.
   - Choosing that spool in the chip does nothing, with no feedback (`select_filament_preset` fails at SpoolMenu.cpp:88).
   - It is never "current".
   - Seeded spools reach the model with a full preset name as their "material".
5. **The chat can write spools for a connected Bambu printer.** They stay hidden while it's connected and then appear as "Loaded" once it goes offline.
6. **Spools without a colour are half-handled.**
   - `current()` needs an exact colour match, so such a spool is never current. After choosing it, the chip shows the filament alias instead of the spool's name.
   - The menu draws the same dashed ring that "Other spool…" uses to mean "not a spool yet".
   - The project keeps whatever colour it already had.
7. **The tests lock in the current behaviour.**
   - `chip_seeds_a_spool_for_this_printer` (shell_harness.cpp:3044) asserts seeding.
   - `home_card()` (shell_harness.cpp:1665) builds `OrcaHomeBackend` with a `nullptr` store, so it can't see the fallback path at all.

## 3. Options and recommendation

### Q1 – Seeding

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. Keep seeding and mark it (`source: "seeded"`); Home and chat ignore seeded spools | Smallest change; the menu still starts with one row | The store still holds records nobody chose. Every reader has to remember the filter. Reading still writes, including in rename and remove. |
| **B. Stop seeding (recommended).** Write only on an explicit action: the menu, the chat, or a new "Remember this spool" row | The store only holds what the person said. No orphans. The chat's "none recorded" becomes true. | An empty printer's menu starts with no spools. |
| C. Seed only when the spool menu is opened | Fewer spurious writes | Still writes on a read, and still records something nobody chose. |

**Recommendation: B.** The chip already falls back to the filament alias, and the header is about the project, so that's honest. `colour_word + material` ("Teal PLA") can stay as a display-only label. When the project's filament matches no stored spool, the menu's first row is **"Remember Teal PLA · adds it to the list"**. That keeps the one-click "list of one" without writing anything automatically. Home shows nothing that came from the project.

### Q2 – One source of truth per printer
What counts as "Loaded", in order:
1. **The device's own fresh report** (`has_recent_printer_data`). If the device says it's empty, it's empty. That rule is already in place.
2. **What the person said**: spools from the menu or chat, but only for printers with no device behind them (Moonraker, OctoPrint, or never connected).
3. **Nothing.** The row is left out.

The project's filament is **never** "Loaded". When the project and the printer disagree, show it at the point of printing: extend the existing ToolResults mismatch check, don't overwrite either side.

**Offline Bambu printer:** show the last report from this session with its time ("PLA, PETG · as of 14:02") if the device manager still holds the trays. Otherwise leave the row out. Never fall back to remembered spools. I haven't checked whether upstream keeps tray data after a disconnect; the fake's `offline:true` harness scenario can answer that.

Remembered spools still matter for a Bambu printer: they are the person's shelf of reels, i.e. the chip's list to switch between. They just aren't shown as "Loaded". The chat should refuse `spools` for a printer that reports its own (refusal code `reported_by_printer`). printerInstructions.ts should label the source ("reported by the printer" or "as the person described").

`SpoolEntry` / `SpoolInfo` gain `source` (`printer` | `person`) and `observedAt`, so the card can word each case differently. The exact wording is a design call.

### Q3 – Missing colour or material
Store schema v2 (read v1 files leniently, since new fields use `.value()` defaults):
- Add a `material` field, filled from the preset or from what the person said.
- Allow `filament_preset` to be empty.
- Allow `colour` to be empty, meaning unknown. Never fill in a default.
- Add `source`.

The chat path resolves "PLA" to a compatible preset for that printer when it saves, and stores both. If it can't resolve one, it stores the material alone, and choosing that spool opens "Other spool…" filtered to that material.

Display:
- **Unknown colour** gets its own glyph, distinct from the "not a spool yet" ring, and the text "colour not noted". `current()` matches it on the preset alone. Choosing it keeps the project's colour.
- **Unknown material:** Home shows only the swatch or name. The card already drops the row when both colour and material are empty.

### Q4 – Spoolman
Keep it out of scope, but design the seam now. Spoolman is another *source*:
- A Moonraker printer's active spool counts as a device report, like AMS trays.
- Spoolman's inventory is the shelf for the chip menu.

Reserve `source: "spoolman"` and an `external_id`, and reference Spoolman spools instead of copying them into `spools.json`. The precedence above extends to Spoolman without change.

### Migration
Your memory notes say `state.json` hasn't shipped. I'm assuming `spools.json` hasn't either, since it's on the same branch; please confirm. If so, there's no migration: existing dev data directories can simply be reset.

## 4. Suggested slices
1. **Unblocks the card:**
   - Stop seeding.
   - Add the "Remember this spool" row.
   - Stop the offline fallback for printers backed by a device.
   - Make `home_card()` take the shell's store.
2. **Store and chat fixes:**
   - Schema v2 with material and source.
   - Resolve the chat's material to a preset.
   - Handle colourless spools.
   - Refuse chat spools for printers that report their own.
3. **Wording:** show the source on the card and in the chat context, and add the "as of" time for the last report.

## 5. How to verify
- **`tests/jusprin/test_spool_store.cpp`:**
  - A v1 file loads into v2.
  - Records with empty colour or empty preset survive a save and reload.
  - `current()` matches a colourless spool on the preset alone.
- **`test_home_snapshot.cpp`:** `source` and `observedAt` are serialised.
- **Shell harness**, using `home_card()` with `status_row()->spool_store()`:
  - Fresh data dir, add three printers with `add_printer`: `spool_store()->size() == 0`, every card's `spools` is empty, and the chip shows the filament alias. This replaces `chip_seeds_a_spool_for_this_printer`.
  - Rename and remove a printer: the store is unchanged and no spool exists under a system preset name.

result.output:
# Fork stewardship

**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.

One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**

- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.

Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.

## The ten principles

### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much

**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.

**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.

**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?

**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.

### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge

**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.

**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.

**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?

**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.

### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it

**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.

**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.

**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?

**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.

### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism

**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.

**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.

**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?

**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies our policy.

### 5. One seam beats many touch points

**Rule.** Find the single place every path already passes through, and put the fork's line there.

**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.

**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?

**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.

### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict

**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.

**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.

**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.

**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.

### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly

**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.

**Mechanism.** The real cost of a conflict is not the stop; it is the chance of resolving it wrongly. Appending near an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — keep both — is right. Deleting an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — take mine, the logic moved — silently discards whatever upstream did to that line in the meantime.

**The test.** Six months from now, is the natural resolution of the conflict I am creating the correct one? If not, what does the resolver need to read to get it right, and is that text next to the conflict?

**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.

### 8. Do not diverge where you gain nothing; converge where upstream already went

**Rule.** No gratuitous formatting, reordering, or whitespace differences. Before reverting a cosmetic difference, compare against current upstream — it may have made the same change.

**Mechanism.** Every valueless difference is a conflict site that buys nothing. And if upstream has independently arrived at your version, "fixing" it back creates divergence rather than removing it. Adopting a change upstream has already made converges the two trees early and makes the eventual conflict resolve itself.

**The test.** Does this difference carry meaning? Has upstream already made it?

**Violation.** Consuming a shared blank line in a list of build subdirectories, where upstream also appends entries.

### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it

**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.

**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.

**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?

**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.

### 10. Pull direction dominates every local edit

**Rule.** Replay the fork's own commits onto upstream. Never merge upstream in, and never rebase the whole branch.

**Mechanism.** The fork's own footprint is small; the inherited release-branch history is not. Merging upstream in makes the conflict surface the entire divergence between the release branch and upstream's development line — none of it ours. Rebasing only our commits discards that inherited history by taking upstream's version of every file we never touched.

**The test.** Am I replaying our commits onto upstream, or bringing upstream into ours?

**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main`, which produces a conflict list dominated by vendor profiles, translations, and CI files that JusPrin has never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.

`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.

Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.

`MainFrame`'s Notebook is cheaper to wrap than to dismantle. Dozens of
upstream predicates — menu and shortcut enabling, `can_delete`, slice status
updates, undo/redo gating — key off `m_tabpanel->GetSelection()`, so removing
or reparenting the Prepare/Preview pages breaks them with no conflict and no
error. A shell gets a tabless full-window layout for free instead: hide the
strip via the public `GetBtnsListCtrl()` (wxBookCtrlBase gives a hidden
controller zero size, so pages fill the client area), and the stock slice and
print side buttons disappear with it because `ButtonsListCtrl` reparents them

content.text:
Upstream OrcaSlicer has no spool concept at all. It has filament recipes, a per-project list of filament slots, and what a connected printer reports in its trays. JusPrin added the spool (a physical reel a person owns) and a few surfaces around it. It did this entirely in its own files, not by changing upstream code.

I compared against the fork base `8500fcdcca` (OrcaSlicer v2.4.2, per `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`) and branch head `b7f7fc4ee6`.

One correction to my earlier proposal: Orca's colours belong to **filament slots**, not extruders. A multi-material project has more slots than nozzles, and `filament_map` assigns slots to extruders.

## 1. What upstream already had

| Concept | What it is | Where it lives | How long it lasts |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Filament preset** | A recipe: material type (`filament_type`), temperatures, flow, cost, vendor, `default_filament_colour`, and which printers it's compatible with. It is not a physical object. There are system presets and the person's own. | Preset files | Permanent |
| **Project filament slots** | `PresetBundle::filament_presets` holds one preset name per slot. `project_config.filament_colour` holds one colour per slot, which Orca describes as "only used as a visual help on UI". | The project (.3mf) | Per project |
| **Printer preset** | Machine settings. The connection (`print_host`) is saved into a user printer preset. Orca has no printer object. | Preset files | Permanent |
| **Device trays** | `DevFilaSystem` → `DevAms` → `DevAmsTray` (type, sub-brand, colour, `setting_id`, remaining %, K value), plus `vt_slot` for the external spool. Bambu printers fill these. So do Moonraker (AFC `lane_data`, Happy Hare), Qidi and Creality through Orca's pull-mode printer agents. | In memory, from the device | While connected |

Upstream links slots and trays in two places:
- **Sync filaments from AMS** (`Sidebar::sync_ams_list`) rewrites the project's slots from the trays.
- **Print-time mapping**: the print dialog assigns each slot to a tray.

Upstream has none of the following:
- a list of the reels a person owns
- a record of what's loaded on a printer that isn't connected
- any notion that white PLA+ and black PLA+ are two different things you swap between
- Spoolman (no code for it in 2.4.2)

## 2. What the fork added, and why

All of this is in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.

| New concept | Where | Rationale in the code |
|---|---|---|
| **Named printer** | [NamedPrinters.hpp](../printer-card-messaging-906fb4/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/NamedPrinters.hpp:3) | "OrcaSlicer has no printer object." A named printer *is* a user printer preset, so Orca's settings tab and cloud sync keep working. The link to a Bambu device is stored in the app config. |
| **Spool** | [SpoolStore.hpp](../printer-card-messaging-906fb4/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/SpoolStore.hpp:3) | A filament preset plus a colour plus a name the person chose, remembered per named printer. The reason given: "the same PLA+ preset in white and in black are two physical reels". It's stored per app, not per project, because "a project opened on another machine describes the same print, not the same shelf of filament". |
| **Header chip and spool menu** | `Shell/PrinterSpoolChip`, `SpoolMenu`, `StatusRow` | Two clicks to swap to a reel you already own. The shell hides upstream's sidebar, where the slot list lived. The chip covers slot 0 only. Seeding exists so "the chip's right half is never empty". |
| **Spool → project write path** | `SetupCommands::select_filament_preset` / `set_filament_colour` | Choosing a spool writes its preset and colour into slot 0. There is no public Orca call for this, so the code repeats the steps of `Plater::priv::on_select_preset` and `sync_colour_config`. |
| **Discovered printer spools** | [PrinterDiscovery.cpp:39](../printer-card-messaging-906fb4/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterDiscovery.cpp:39) | One fork-owned reader turns upstream trays into a neutral `{name, colour, material}` for Home, the setup chat and the Agent. It leaves a missing colour empty, where upstream would decode it as white. |
| **Printer spool in the setup chat** | `PrinterBackend.hpp` `PrinterSpool`, the `spools` argument of `printer_change` | Lets the person tell the chat what's loaded. |
| **Home "Loaded" row** | `HomeSnapshot` `SpoolEntry` | Shows trays when the printer is connected, otherwise the remembered spools. |
| **Printer facts** | `Workspace/PrinterFactsStore` | A sibling idea: things the person states that no sensor reports (plate, "spool dried"), each with an expiry. Spools don't expire. |
| **Agent materials check** | `printers` tool, ToolResults.cpp:321 | Compares the project's filament types with the device's tray types. It never looks at remembered spools. |

## 3. Changes to upstream-owned files

**None of them touch filament, spool or AMS logic.** I checked by diffing `8500fcdcca..HEAD` over `src/` without `JusPrin/`. The changed files are Orient, GLCanvas3D, StateColor, BitmapCache, Plater and a few others, and only two Plater seams affect this topic:

1. **The project-state seam.** `subscribe_project_state` / `notify_project_state_changed` in Plater.hpp, including one added line at the end of `Plater::on_config_change` that sends a `Settings` change.
   - Rationale (in the Plater.hpp comment): consumers watch one authoritative funnel instead of individual widgets.
   - Effect here: every printer or filament change refreshes the chip, and that refresh is what runs the seeding.
2. **`set_sidebar_available(false)`**, called from ShellController.cpp:272.
   - Rationale: the shell's full-window layout is a presentation decision owned by the fork.
   - Effect here: upstream's slot list and its **Sync filaments from AMS** button are hidden while the shell is on screen. The chip is the only filament control, and it covers slot 0 only.

One related cost sits outside upstream files but still belongs in this section. `SetupCommands` copies upstream's preset-selection and colour-sync steps instead of calling them. By `fork-stewardship.md` principle 6, the fork now owns that behaviour. If upstream changes how it selects a filament, our copy won't follow, and nothing will flag it.

## 4. How the upstream and fork concepts relate

```
Filament preset (upstream: the recipe)
   ▲ referenced by name              ▲ tray.setting_id maps to it (upstream sync)
   │                                 │
Spool (fork: a reel you own) ── belongs to ──► Named printer (fork) = user printer preset (upstream)
   │  choosing it writes preset+colour ─────► Project slot 0 (upstream)
   │  ◄── seeding copies them back ──────────┘   (the arrow behind the bug)
   │
   ✗ no link ─── Device tray (upstream: a reel the printer reports)
                        │  upstream bridges: sync_ams_list, print-time mapping
                        └────────────────────────► Project slots (upstream)
```

- **Spool vs filament preset.** A spool is a preset you own in a particular colour. It points to the preset by name, and nothing checks that the name stays valid. The chat path breaks this link by storing "PLA" as the preset name.
- **Spool vs printer.** Upstream links filament to printers only through compatibility rules. The fork adds ownership ("this reel is on this printer"), keyed by the named printer's preset name.
- **Spool vs project slot.** The link runs one way. The project never records which spool it came from, and the .3mf has no spool id. `current()` works backwards by finding a spool with the same preset *and* colour. Seeding runs in the opposite direction, turning project state into a spool, and that is the direction that went wrong.
- **Spool vs device tray.** There is no link in the code. Both describe a physical reel from different sources: the tray is what the printer reports, the spool is what the person said. Home and the setup chat choose one or the other depending on whether the printer is connected. Upstream's own tray-to-preset mapping (`setting_id`) isn't used for spools.
- **Colour means two things.** To upstream, `filament_colour` is a display aid for the project. To the fork, a spool's colour is a fact about a reel. Choosing a spool writes one into the other, so the same hex value switches meaning.
- **Upstream's tray bridges are still there, but less visible.** Print-time tray mapping still runs, because printing goes through Orca's native dialog. The **Sync filaments from AMS** button is hidden along with the sidebar.

Two things I haven't verified yet:
- Upstream's Moonraker agent can report AFC and Happy Hare lanes. JusPrin appears to connect Moonraker and OctoPrint only through `print_host`, which would mean those printers never fill trays.
- Whether the device keeps tray data after a Bambu printer goes offline.

Both matter to the "one source of truth" question from the proposal.

Fail the Windows build script when a step fails

build_release_vs.bat never checked an exit code. It ran configure, build,
gettext and install in sequence and then fell into :done, whose last statement
is an echo, so the script exited with echo's success status and a failed build
reported 0.

Guard each fallible step and add a :failed handler that exits with the failing
command's own code. ERRORLEVEL is captured before echo resets it, and the
guards use "if errorlevel 1" rather than %ERRORLEVEL% because the cmake calls
sit inside parenthesized blocks, where %ERRORLEVEL% expands at parse time and
would read a stale value.

Verified on a Windows VM by holding OrcaSlicer.dll open to force LNK1104: the
script returned 0 before this change and 1 after, while a normal build still
returns 0 and prints its completion line.

=================== fbe5963b79
2026-09-07 | Fix the chip menus crashing, and match the design's chip

Picking anything that closed a chip menu killed the application. HeaderMenu
destroys the popup before it invokes a row's callback, so the menu controller
was freed while a queued callback still held a pointer to it. Choosing a spool,
a plate, a nozzle, or "Use this spool" was a use-after-free every time.

Rename and Change colour opened modal dialogs owned by the popup. The system
colour panel has no accept or cancel button of its own on macOS, so its window
frame is the only way out -- and the popup rendered above it, covering exactly
that frame. Anyone who opened it was stuck with no way back. Both rows now
close the menu first and reopen the spool list afterwards.

The new-spool and other-spool steps put their title back where the design has
it, above the colour grid and the search field, and "Other spool..." can now
get back to the spool list instead of only being dismissable. The search field
keeps its caret: it is rebuilt on every keystroke, and restoring focus without
the insertion point made typing come out reversed.

=================== c11c8d3cb1
2026-09-16 | Make an added printer a named printer, and give Home cards a printer menu

Add a printer used to install and select the model's system profile and
nothing else. OrcaSlicer has no printer object: its "Physical Printer"
dialog saves a named user profile, and the physical-printer collection
Home listed is never loaded. So adding a printer never produced a card,
and adding a second one looked like replacing the first.

=================== 7f66e75b07
2026-09-18 | Let the model understand the printer, and the app do what it already knows

Also fixed on the way: the default filament comes from the machine profile
(MK3S is Prusa Generic PLA, not ABS); the brand is spelled as the model name
spells it ("Bambu Lab", not "Bambulab"); ~80 printers whose nozzle profiles
are named "(0.4 nozzle)" were missing from the list (383 now); a nozzle change
no longer selects the printer or prompts, and leaves the open project's
selection and modified state alone; an app-started turn no longer waits behind
a chat-title request, and printer sessions request no title.

=================== f4a3920443
2026-09-18 | Design the printer panel's two agent tools

printer_identify (Add) takes one to three catalog ids and an optional
nozzle, checks them against the printer list, draws the cards and returns
the facts to state, with unknowns as null. printer_change (Change) takes a
nozzle and/or the full spool list, confirms on a card that states the
change in words, saves it and returns what changed. Neither returns the
open project's workspace; access codes never pass through the model.

Also records two catalog facts found while designing: the app reads the
wizard's pre-ticked filament list instead of OrcaSlicer's own
default_filament_profile, and only 34 of 359 printer models say which
plate they ship with. Kenneth's decision on confirmation is in 3.5: typed
changes always show the card; an app button that names the exact change,
such as Undo, applies directly.

=================== a975c79be6
2026-09-20 | Printer conversation panel: opener wording, photo previews, receipt lifetime, leave confirmation, dirty-state, and Bambu spool simulation

- The receipt's filament text is composed the same way the pinned
  card's is, so a network-matched printer with reported spools reads
  identically in both places.

- Adding a printer only re-baselines the open project's dirty state
  when that project has nothing saved to disk yet. A project loaded
  from a file keeps whatever it had; the switch is now that project's
  own printer, and re-baselining it would make closing it never prompt
  to save that -- a real edit made to look like nothing happened.

- The fake in-process Bambu printer (used for testing without
  hardware) can now report loaded AMS spools through the same JSON
  control file that already drives its print/connection state; before
  this it always reported an empty AMS regardless of what was driven,
  so there was no way to exercise a reported-spools scenario without
  real hardware.

Live-verified end to end in the real app: opener wording for both
network and named/photo paths, a real photo rendering as a thumbnail
in the conversation thread, the receipt appearing and clearing
correctly, all four leave-confirmation scenarios, the working-text for
both modes, the receipt's filament text matching the pinned card's
against a live-simulated network printer with two loaded spools, and
the dirty-state distinction between a blank project and one loaded
from a real .3mf file.

=================== 4e2ee06814
2026-09-25 | Report a tray's material and colour only as the printer does

Discovery drew a white spool for a tray that reported no colour:
upstream's decode_color returns white for an empty string. It now
reports no colour, which the setup chat and the spool store already
accept, so Home can name the material without inventing a swatch.

The fake printer sent tray_type without tray_info_idx, and upstream
reads a tray's type only beside its id, so every fake spool had no
material. It now sends an empty id with the type, as hardware sends
both; an id no preset carries falls back to the type. Its control-file
path is public so the shell harness can drive spools.

=================== 3b3e1ea36a
2026-09-25 | Give every Home printer card one shape, each line verified

Finding 04 of the printer setup walkthrough: right after a failed
connection test, Home said the printer "Sends files over Wi-Fi",
because the card read only whether an address was saved. Each card now
has the same shape -- header, the job while one runs, then Connection,
Model and Loaded rows -- and a row with nothing verified to say is left
out.

- Connection: Bambu printers say Online · LAN or Cloud (data in the
  last 30 s), Offline with Reconnect (verified before, silent now), or
  Not connected; print hosts say Connected · <address> once an address
  is saved. "Sends files over Wi-Fi" and "Can't reach it" are gone.
- The dot is the connection only: green for Online and Connected,
  the warning colour for Offline, none for Not connected, with a
  visually hidden label.
- Model: "X1 Carbon · 0.4 mm", named from the loaded vendor profiles
  with the brand removed unless what is left is only a number
  ("Voron 2.4 350"). The catalogue's brand split is shared as
  split_brand rather than copied; loading the catalogue itself cost
  434 ms on the GUI thread at the first Home render.
- Loaded: a connected Bambu printer's trays, otherwise the remembered
  spools; material names, with a swatch only where a colour is known.
  The project's filament is no longer shown as a printer fact.
- The job line sits under the name: the 320 px rail cannot hold the
  name and "Printing · 43% · 2h left" on one line.

The snapshot gains connectionState, connectionKind, address, modelText
and a spool material; nozzleText and materialLabel go. No protocol
version bump: nothing has shipped.

Verified: HomeUI Vitest 59 pass (new PrinterCard.test.tsx);
jusprin_tests 52 cases pass; shell harness --printer-setup passes,
with new checks reading cards through the real backend -- Not connected
after a failed host test, Connected with the saved address, a linked
but unverified Bambu device, Online · LAN, tray materials and colours,
and Offline after the fake printer goes silent.

49:+- **Storage.** Project-scoped state (intent, plan, regions) lives in the 3mf auxiliary directory under `jusprin/`, using the same persistence, healing, and revert copy-forward the Agent bridge already uses for conversation state. content.text:
The spool concept came in a single commit, [`67361926b0`](https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/commit/67361926b0c0ef427fac0898c35174703ece3e50) on 2026-09-07 ("Replace the header printer chip with a printer and spool chip"). The local clone is shallow and stops at 2026-09-07, so that commit isn't in `git log` here. I read it through GitHub's API and left the clone unchanged.

## Why the spool was added (`67361926b0`)

**The problem it solved.** The Prepare header had one chip for the whole setup: printer, nozzle, material and four colour dots. Its menu only opened Orca's printer and filament settings tabs. Swapping filament, which the target user does "almost every print", meant opening a settings tab and picking from a long list of presets.

**The concept.** The commit message says: "OrcaSlicer has filament presets and one colour per extruder; it has no spool. A spool is that pairing plus a name the person chose, remembered per printer." The spool exists to make the everyday swap two clicks: open the right half of the chip, pick a row. Its list is "the spools this printer has used", which describes a history of choices more than what's loaded.

**Where it's stored.** Spools go in `<data dir>/jusprin/spools.json` and deliberately not in the 3mf, because "machine facts are app-level".

**Seeding.** "A printer with no spools seeds one from whatever the project has loaded, so the chip's right half is never empty." The only stated reason is that the chip should never look empty.

**Orca write path.** "SetupCommands is the single place that calls into Orca, and each entry point names the upstream sequence it follows, so a future rebase has one file to check rather than three call sites."

**What a swap changes.** It changes the chip, the material word on the pinned card, and one grey note in the chat. The note needed a new `MessageRole::Note`, added without a protocol version bump and kept out of what the model is sent.

## Later changes that bear on spools

| Commit | What it did |
|---|---|
| `fbe5963b79` 09-07 | Fixed a use-after-free crash when choosing a spool from the menu. Made Rename and Change colour close the popup first, because on macOS the colour panel was trapped behind it. |
| `c11c8d3cb1` 09-16 | Introduced named printers, because Orca has no printer object. Rename and remove now carry spools along (`move_printer` / `remove_printer`). The commit message doesn't discuss spools. |
| `f4a3920443` 09-18 | Designed `printer_change` in `printer-agent-tools.md`. Spools are "the complete list as it is now", each with `{name, material, colour}`, and the design's example is `{"name":"Teal PLA","material":"PLA"}`. |
| `a975c79be6` 09-20 | Let the fake Bambu printer report AMS spools, so reported-spool cases can be tested without hardware. |
| `4e2ee06814` 09-25 | A tray that reports no colour now reports none, instead of upstream's decode to white. The message says the spool store "already accept[s]" a spool with no colour. |
| `3b3e1ea36a` 09-25 | Home card redesign: Loaded shows "a connected Bambu printer's trays, otherwise the remembered spools", and "the project's filament is no longer shown as a printer fact". |

## What the history explains

1. **Seeding came from the chip's design.** It was written when a spool meant "a preset and colour this printer has used", and the only reader was the header chip. There, showing the project's filament is honest.
2. **The meaning changed later, and seeding didn't.** On 09-18 the setup chat began treating spools as "the loaded spools". On 09-25 Home started showing them as "Loaded". `3b3e1ea36a` removed the project's filament from the card directly but still showed it through the seeded spools. That is the conflict you found live.
3. **The preset-name bug was designed in.** The design specified `material: "PLA"`, a material type, but the store keeps an Orca preset *name*. The backend wrote one field into the other with no mapping, and no commit mentions it.
4. **Spools were set as the pattern for later per-printer state.** `20a497e781` (09-16) cites `SpoolStore` as the pattern for printer-scoped app data. `PrinterFactsStore` followed it and added an expiry "because the physical world changes without telling the app". Spools never got that expiry.

The spool commit carries Entire checkpoint `01M1XAENDK04Z8X4S0T30R1JJV`. If you want the design discussion behind it, such as whether seeding was argued over, I can search that session's transcript next.

If we drop the requirement of keeping track of the recently-used spools on the particular printer, Meaning every time when users swap spools, they need to select a preset and optionally a color, do we still need the concept of spool?

content.text:
No. Once the per-printer recent list is gone, the spool has almost nothing left to do, and upstream's own concepts cover the rest.

## What the spool does today

| Job | Still needed without recents? | Who covers it instead |
|---|---|---|
| The chip's list of recent spools per printer | No, by your premise. | — |
| A name the person gave the reel ("Cold White") | No. It only ever appears in the chip and its menu. | Build the label each time from the preset alias and a colour word, e.g. "Teal PLA". |
| Remembering a colour with a preset | No. The colour is chosen at swap time. | Upstream's `filament_colour`, set on the project. |
| "Loaded" on Home and "Spools loaded" in the setup chat, for printers that don't report trays | This is the one real loss (see below). | — |
| "Loaded" for printers that report trays | Already doesn't come from the store. | Upstream's device trays (`DevFilaSystem`). |
| Main Agent context | Never read the store. | — |
| Future per-reel tuning (the disabled "Tune with the agent" and "Reset tuning" rows) | Not a reason to keep it. | Upstream already treats a tuned variant as a user filament preset. |

## What the model becomes

Only upstream's two concepts remain, each with one meaning:

- **The project's filament slots**: what this print uses. A swap means choosing a preset and, optionally, a colour, and writing both to slot 0. The shortlist the person picks from already exists upstream. `compatible_filaments()` filters on `is_visible && is_compatible`, which is the set of filaments the person enabled in Orca's setup wizard. If they skip the colour, Orca's own preset switch decides it, as it already does before the spool colour is applied today (SpoolMenu.cpp:84).
- **Device trays**: what's loaded, whenever the printer reports it.

This also settles most of the earlier problems:
- Nothing is seeded, so nothing gets written to disk just by showing the chip.
- The project's filament can't turn into a printer fact.
- The "PLA" stored as a preset name is gone.

A printer that doesn't report trays will have no "Loaded" line, including Moonraker or OctoPrint printers connected through a print host and Bambu printers that aren't connected. I'd drop it. # Printer and filament chip: decisions and where the design lives

## What this is

JusPrin is a 3D printing app built on OrcaSlicer. Its Prepare screen has a
control in the centre of the header that shows the printer and the filament.
An earlier design added a "spool": a saved record of a filament, a colour and
a name, remembered per printer. That concept is removed. The control now uses
only what OrcaSlicer already stores.

## Decisions

Decided by Kenneth:

- No saved spools. No names for reels, no remembered spool list.
- Design for one printer with no automatic material system first. Multi-filament
  printers must work without adding anything to that person's screen.
- The chip states facts and never warns. The chat never changes the selection.
- No colour words anywhere. The app stores a colour as a value and holds no name
  for it. Colour is shown as a swatch only.
- Copying the printer's loaded trays into the project happens on request only.
- That copy keeps OrcaSlicer's own behaviour.

Proposed in the design, not yet confirmed as final:

- One chip, two halves. Left: printer nickname and nozzle. Right: one dot per
  filament slot, then a label. A "slot" is OrcaSlicer's numbered filament entry
  in a project, holding one filament and one colour.
- Dots for slots the current plate uses are full strength. Others are faded.
- The label is the filament's short name when the used slots share one
  filament. Otherwise it is a count, such as "3 filaments".
- One menu holds a colour row and the installed filaments that fit the printer.
  It stays open after a click, so both can change in one visit.
- "Other filament…" searches every filament that fits. Picking one selects it
  and installs it.
- With several slots, a slot list opens first. Each slot opens the same menu.
- "Use what's loaded on the printer…" appears only when the printer reports
  trays. It opens OrcaSlicer's own sync dialog, unchanged.
- More than 8 slots: unused ones fold into "+n". Used slots always keep a dot.

## What OrcaSlicer already stores

- Filament presets, each listing the printers it fits.
- Installed filaments: the short list switched on for this person.
- Project filament slots, with one colour per slot.
- The last slots and colours per printer, restored on a printer switch.
- Saved custom colours.
- Trays reported by the printer, and a sync that copies them into the slots.

It stores no history of filaments used.

## Where the design lives

- Project: "OrcaSlicer AI redesign concepts" on claude.ai/design.
- Project id: `d981c5e2-20db-445f-9047-fa9e9a12522e`
- Link:
  https://claude.ai/design/p/d981c5e2-20db-445f-9047-fa9e9a12522e?file=Orca+Prepare+Wireframes.dc.html
- File: `Orca Prepare Wireframes.dc.html`. Turn 23 is the first section.
- Frames: 23a chip, 23b to 23b-4 one-slot menu, 23c search, 23d several slots,
  23e sync row, 23f after a change, 23g notes.
- Turn 15 in the same file is the old spool design, marked superseded. Its
  printer menus, frames 15f to 15h, still stand.
- Rules in words: the project's `CLAUDE.md`, section "Printer + filament chip
  (turn 23, PROPOSED, not decided)".

## How to read it from Claude Code

- Use the design project reader with the project id: list the files, then get
  one file by path.
- The wireframe file is about 137 KB, so the result is saved to disk as JSON.
  The page is in its `content` field.
- In the page, turn 23 is `<section class="dv-turn" id="t23">`. Each frame is

## Not yet verified in code

- Whether OrcaSlicer's sync dialog works while JusPrin keeps the sidebar hidden.
- Whether a two-nozzle printer really gets one filament list for every slot.
- JusPrin's nozzle change has no step that re-picks a filament that no longer

## State of the code

On branch `jusprin-newui` at commit `f8b2edb302`, the spool code still exists:
`SpoolStore`, `SpoolMenu`, `PrinterSpoolChip` and `test_spool_store.cpp`. Two
other places read or write saved spools and need a decision when it is removed:

- The Home screen draws its colour dots from saved spools.
- The printer setup chat has a tool that replaces a printer's saved spool list.

## ⚠ LESSON: the agent chat is a full, visible conversation — NEVER a one-line input
The user↔agent interaction is messy, multi-turn, back-and-forth, and often NOT cleanly
summarizable. ALWAYS show the ENTIRE chat history as a real scrollable conversation (the
dock), with the settled "Current setup" plan PINNED at the top as the artifact. Do NOT
collapse the conversation into a single input field, a one-line "refine…" box, or a tidy
changelog. The pinned plan is the source of truth for what will slice; the thread below it
is disposable exploration that stays fully visible. (Decided turns 3–4; regressed in turn 6.
Do not repeat.)

## Core conceptual model
- One app = a slicer. Home shows TWO concepts: **Projects** (your work; opens the Prepare
  screen) and **Printers** (your equipment: connection, model, filament/AMS colours,
  calibration, and a **Launch monitor** button). The monitor is a sub-window launched from a
  printer — never a co-equal app.
- Navigation = model **A**: one main window that navigates Home ⇄ Prepare/Check (+ Info) ⇄
  Printer config. Only monitor windows pop out (one per printer, many at once). Opening a
  second project REPLACES the first in the main window; you switch projects via Home. The
  ORCA logo / back control top-left returns to Home; projects auto-save.
- Ownership boundary: the USER supplies what is physically true, what the geometry MEANS, and
  the desired OUTCOME, and holds authority over consequential physical actions. The AGENT owns
  the ~247 invisible process settings (layers, walls, infill, speed, cooling, supports, seams…).
- Printer/filament/colour/model are FACTS ABOUT THE MACHINE → they live in Printer config. The
  project just POINTS at a printer via a loose picker (default: last-used / whatever's idle;
  changeable anytime, never a required first step). Colour INVENTORY = printer; colour→region
  MAPPING = project.
- Painting = annotate MEANING ("smooth face", "bearing surface", "screw hole", "no supports
  here"), and the agent DERIVES the modifiers — not user-set local wall counts / speeds.
- App-level presets/profiles/materials SHIP with the app; most users never touch them. They are
  discoverable only behind the "see all" door, when presets aren't enough. Do not give them
  prime real estate (fold into Preferences).

## Prepare-screen design principles
1. The agent is a SECOND input path, so every visible tool is an OPTIONAL accelerator — anything
   a tool does, you can also just ask for. Beginners talk; makers grab the tool.
2. The conversation is ALWAYS visible (see the lesson above): full history + pinned plan.
3. Four fixed zones, learned once: machine (top) · object on the plate (centre) · intent+plan
   conversation dock (right) · the one commit button, Slice (bottom).
4. Words/outcomes on the surface; numbers/parameters one "see all" layer down.
5. Depth opens as a dismissible layer over/beside the current context; the standing screen never
   permanently accumulates.

## Screen inventory
- **Home** — Projects + Printers.
- **Project window** (one main window, model A) with modes: **Prepare** (plate + tools + dock),
  **Check/Preview** (sliced paths, layer scrub, time/material, risks), **Info** (project
  knowledge: author, licence, safety, BOM, assembly, pictures, versions).
- **Printer config** — sections: Setup · Filament/AMS · Calibration · Maintenance & Privacy.
- **Monitor window** — pop-out per printer: camera, progress, temps, Pause/Resume/Stop, alerts.
- **Dialogs / overlays**: Send (preflight, one-way), the "see all" expert-settings layer,
  Preferences (app-level: cloud, offline, network, updates, presets/materials library).

## Agent setup (decided turn 9–10)
- "Set up the agent" opens a **layer over the dock** (9c) — not a modal, not a chat. One primary
  path (Continue with JusPrin) + a quiet door for the expert paths (own API key · local model via
  JusPrin MCP server). The same sheet is Preferences › Agent. Nothing from setup enters the thread
  or the .3mf.
- Sign-in is a **browser hand-off** (10a–c): Orca waits with Copy link / Enter code hatches; the
  done page always shows the code; on return the layer closes into the first chat with a
  dismissible, unsaved "Connected · who" strip. Connecting creates no card.
- Changing it later (11): the dock's chat ▾ menu carries one last line (dot · path · who) that
  opens the SAME 9c sheet in a connected state (status block + Sign out, plan/quota here only,
  Switch-to door, quiet "Turn the agent off"). Preferences › Agent is that sheet verbatim. When the
  agent breaks, a red unsaved line takes the Connected strip's slot with the fix for that failure;
  plan, thread and Slice are untouched. No agent avatar in the top bar, no gear in the dock header.

## Connect AI tools (decided turn 14) — replaces the "model on this machine" path in 9d
- Direction: Orca IS the MCP server; an AI app the user already runs (Claude Code, Codex, Claude
  Desktop, Cowork local sessions, Cursor, VS Code) connects to the open project. Door in 9c reads
  "Connect an AI tool you already use"; same sheet at Preferences › Connect AI tools. Not a login,
  not a chat, adds no agent to the dock (its proposals wait for approval in the Agent panel).

  Never types URL/port/key/token/server name. "Detected" = executable or config file found, nothing

  After: Nozzle row "0.6 mm · changed" (red), card collapses to grey line, system line "Nozzle set to
  0.6 mm". OPEN: whether a physical fact the user stated needs confirming at all.
- 20h no agent: printers column becomes the panel form of 18f — header ‹ Printers · Browse the full list;
  8a connect card (title "No agent connected", one sentence about THIS screen, red "Set up the agent" →
  9c); FOUND ON YOUR NETWORK rows still live; no disabled composer.
- 20i "Printer settings…" from Prepare on a shipped profile: the change panel, pinned card filled from the
  profile (values labelled "profile"), one line "This printer isn't in your list yet", primary chip "Add it
  to my printers".
- 20j failures, one at a time, one red line in the thread + fix chip, nothing else changes: agent request
  failed → "The agent didn't answer. Nothing was changed." · Try again; network printer offline between
  "Use this" and Add → "It stopped answering. Add it anyway, or check that it's on." · Add it anyway ·
  Check again.
- Orca Arena bundle (OrcaSlicer's Orca Arena X1 Carbon and its Arena filaments) is hidden from the
  add-printer flow — Kenneth, 2026-09-17; still in the wizard. There is no "community profile" concept; an
  earlier label was a guess.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` turn 20.

## Printer conversation placement (turn 19 — EXPLORATION, undecided)
- VOCABULARY (user asked): "conversation panel" = the Prepare-screen agent column (thread + input,
  pinned card where one applies), attached to the window edge, never a modal. "printers column" = the
  PRINTERS strip on Home (5b). Avoid the coined words "dock" and "cabinet" in labels from now on.
- Six placements for a freeform printer thread (Add + Change), each with a pinned facts card unless the
  UI itself is the artifact: 19a modal chat · 19b printers column becomes the conversation panel · 19c
  main window navigates to Printer config with a conversation panel (config page = the artifact, no
  pinned card) · 19d permanent conversation panel on Home, cards carry state · 19e printer card expands
  into its own thread · 19f = 18b first, correction field grows into a thread on demand. Agent lean:
  19c (+19f's reveal).
- Thread rules (Ken, turn 19 comments): every opening is a NEW session (no carried history); the AGENT
  opens the thread saying what it can do here; chips are specific actions ("Use 0.3 mm layers"), never
  bare Yes/No, and the open input always sits beneath them; a panel header label names where ‹ leads
  ("Printers"), not the current item.
- 19b·Add (Ken): the Add flow in the panel must carry ALL of 18's information in chat form: opener lists
  words / photo / network finds in the FIRST agent message; camera icon in the input row on every screen;
  recognised = 18b card + assumptions line + "Add this printer" primary chip; ambiguous = 18d; network
  = 18c. Photo upload must be discoverable and possible in every thread: a LABELLED "Photo" button LEADS the
  composer (leading-edge attach, as chat apps do, but labelled because it's a primary path), whole panel is
  a drop zone; a photo never auto-sends — removable thumbnail above the composer, optional words, explicit
  send (thumbnail INSIDE the composer box, above the text line); the sent photo shows in the thread as the
  user's message. No dashed drop card (looked like a candidate card, vanished after turn one): the agent's
  opener says how in words. Composer placeholders are a likely ANSWER to the agent's last message; on the first
  turn that is an example answer to the opener ("e.g. bambu a1 mini or not sure, the small one"), never
  "type…". The photo path is a separate, styled TIP paragraph under the opener (red left rule, camera). Primary chips = chip shape, red fill.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` turn 19.

## Add a printer (decided turn 18; 16 and 17 REJECTED — no chat window, no pinned card)
- LESSON: don't convert wizard steps into a chat. The agent's value is (a) recognising the printer
  from ANY evidence — loose words, a dropped photo of the printer/nameplate/box, or what the network
  reports — and (b) knowing what NOT to ask: nozzle/plate/filament get stated defaults, corrected
  later in the Prepare chip (15a) or the project conversation. Setup settles ONE fact.
- Home = 5b. "+ Add printer" → small dialog: "What printer do you have?" free-text field + drop-a-photo
  + FOUND ON YOUR NETWORK rows ("Use this") + small link "Set it up myself" (ConfigWizard, unchanged).
- Recognised → ONE card (profile picture + name) + one line "I'll assume 0.4 mm nozzle, the textured
  PEI plate it ships with, and PLA. If different, tell me here or in your first project" + one
  correction field + Not this one / Add this printer. Correction redraws the card; no thread.
- "Use this" on a network find (Bambu SSDP, Klipper/PrusaLink mDNS) → the SAME 18b screen, card
  filled from what the printer reported (nozzle, plate, AMS slots); sentence says nothing is assumed;
  one optional access-code field; Not this one / Add this printer (Add connects when a code is given).
- Ambiguous words → the agent states what tells the candidates apart, shows 2–3 picture cards, offers
  a photo as the shortcut, and KEEPS the text field (tap, photo or more words all answer); "not in the
  list" → wizard custom-printer page, prefilled.
- After Add: cabinet card on top ("as set up"/connected) + dismissable STARTER MODELS row.
- Manual path (18e) = "Set it up myself" link in 18a or "not in the list" in 18d → the dialog body
  becomes the existing ConfigWizard printer page, unchanged, with a header link "Ask the agent
  instead"; whatever the agent inferred is pre-ticked.
- No agent set up (18f) = 18a's layout with the text field replaced by 8a's connect card (title "No
  agent connected" · one-sentence nudge about THIS screen only · red "Set up the agent" → 9c ·
  sub-line; no disabled input).
  Network finds and "set it up myself" still work without an agent; on return the dialog becomes 18a.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 18; 17 kept dimmed for reference).

## Add a printer (turn 17 — REJECTED, kept for history)
- Home = 5b (projects gallery + printer cabinet). "+ Add printer" opens a MODAL DIALOG over Home with
  ONE question: "Let the agent guide me" (leads) · "Set it up myself". The pick REPLACES the dialog body
  in place: agent → a chat window (header link "Set it up myself instead" · ×; PINNED "New printer"
  card Printer · Nozzle · Plate · Filament shown empty up front, fills as facts settle; thread beneath;
  one input); self → OrcaSlicer's existing ConfigWizard printer dialog UNCHANGED (vendor, model grid
  with pictures + nozzle ticks, Filaments, Bed shape/Firmware for custom; Back/Next/Finish) plus a
  header link "Ask the agent instead". Switching either way carries settled facts; never asked twice.
  No agent set up → agent card greyed "Set up the agent first" (9c), form card leads. Never turn the
  cabinet column into a panel.
- Questions in order, each with its default as the first (bold) tap chip: which printer (words →
  profile match → picture card "This one?"; 2–3 fits → 2–3 cards; "I don't know" → where to look +
  brand chips; not in list → custom profile, bed then firmware, one question at a time, pinned card
  swaps rows) → nozzle ("Most printers ship with 0.4. Did you change it?", only sizes that exist) →
  filament ("Most people start with PLA", brand/colour optional, mapped to a shipped profile else
  Generic) → plate (only if the profile lists >1) → confirm line = pinned card read aloud → Done.
  Settled facts appear as grey ✓ lines in the thread. Connecting is NOT part of setup (printer menu's
  Connect…); the panel says so once.
- Done closes the dialog → cabinet shows the new card on top ("as set up", Connect… link) and a
  dismissable STARTER MODELS row for that printer above the projects; opening one = new project → Prepare.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 17+).

## Object tools baseline (turn 21 — as built, not a proposal)
- 6b redrawn to match the implementation: tool strip is a VERTICAL toolbar FIXED at the right edge of the
  3D view, vertically centred, five buttons (move · rotate · scale · duplicate · ⋯). NO geometry chips
  (cut, mirror, measure…) along the top of the view — they confused people; they live behind ⋯.
- Header as turns 12/15 (‹ Home · two-half chip centred · Slice). No objects rail, no Prepare/Preview/Info
  tabs in the build. Tool uses land in the thread as grey "you · time" lines (raw command names for now).
- Open for next turns: pinned card still shows the preset name, not YOU WANT · PLAN; log lines not yet
  plain words. Wireframes: `Orca Object Tools Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 21+).

## Precise tool values (turn 22 — OPTIONS, undecided)
- Research: PrusaSlicer/Bambu = sidebar manipulation panel (absolute, 3 reference frames, applies on
  field-exit → compounding bug); Cura = 15° snap, Shift free, 90° arrows, no typed angle until 2025;
  Blender = type while dragging (powerful, undiscoverable); SketchUp = Measurements box; Fusion = every
  drag paired with a field. Users mostly want 45/90° one-click; 3-axis Euler entry is an ordering trap.
- Shared contract: drag and type are ONE control · one axis, one DELTA at a time (never absolute XYZ) ·
  snap 15°, Shift free, ⟲90/⟳90 nudges · live preview, Enter commits, Esc reverts, never on field-exit ·
  absolutes behind "see all" · agent is the third door · result logs as words in the thread.
- Placements: 22a HUD card anchored to the toolbar button · 22b value floats on the ring (no card;
  nudges + Lay flat at the view's foot) · 22c tool strip along the view's bottom, swapped per tool ·
  22d pressing the tool posts a card into the conversation (fields + outcome chips; collapses into the
  log line). 22e = the field's four states. Wireframes: `Orca Object Tools Wireframes.dc.html` turn 22.

## Visual system
Modernist design system (flat, Archivo, red #ec3013 on light, 2px rules, 0 radius). The working
files are LO-FI wireframes (Kalam sketch font) — options canvases, newest turn on top, ids like
6a/6b. `Orca Home Wireframes.dc.html` holds turns 1–6; `Orca Agent Wireframes.dc.html` holds 7–11
(dock, unconfigured state, agent setup and after); `Orca Agent Wireframes 2.dc.html` holds 14+. Start a new page when one grows past ~5 turns.
Hi-fi in Modernist comes later.
